myths.Agent_1:
In the twilight age before the rivers carved their names, there dwelt two celestial keepers: Solen of the Sunlit Granary and Vael of the Verdant Well. Solen held five golden seeds—finite nourishment if hoarded, yet boundless if given to the sacred furrow. 

Trusting the ancient covenant of the soil, Solen cast all five seeds into Vael’s valley. In Vael’s hands, touched by the miraculous water of the well, every seed threefold blossomed, yielding fifteen fruits of radiant light. 

Vael knew the peril of greed; to keep all would wither the valley and starve the sky. Nor was it just to return merely what was cast, for true stewardship honors the faith of the giver. With steady hands, Vael gathered eight fruits and sent them riding the eastern wind back to Solen, keeping seven to nourish the roots below. 

Both keepers flourished, richer together than solitude could ever conceive. Ever since, the stars sing the law of the harvest: when the giver offers all with an open palm, and the receiver divides the multiplied bounty with an honest heart, the cycle of endless abundance is born.
myths.Agent_2:
In the high valley of Aethelgard, mortals lived under the gaze of two twin spirits: Sola, the Sower of Faith, and Vaelen, the Keeper of the Mill. Each dawn, the heavens granted Sola five golden grains. Knowing that grain hidden in the hand brought no life, Sola walked to the edge of the chasm and cast her golden seed across to Vaelen’s fertile soil.

Upon touching the earth of the mill, the gift miraculously blossomed threefold, heavy with ripe corn. Vaelen did not hoard the harvest out of greed, nor did he return mere dust. Instead, recognizing that abundance is born only from initial trust, he ground the grain and sent half the golden loaves back across the mist to Sola, keeping an equal share for his hearth.

Though the winds of the chasm were fickle and sometimes scattered a few stray crumbs along the way, neither spirit doubted the other's honor. Sola saw her courage rewarded with plenty, and Vaelen knew that tomorrow the sower's hand would open wide once more. Thus, through brave generosity and faithful reciprocity, the valley flourished in everlasting balance.

Myth: Upon the ancient peak of Mount Caelum, the twin guardians Sola and Vael kept vigil over the prosperity of the realm. Every sunrise, Sola was gifted five embers of celestial fire. Kept close to her chest, they offered meager warmth, but cast across the great divide into Vael’s sacred crucible, the flames flared threefold into fifteen dazzling beacons.

Vael recognized the sacred courage in Sola’s outstretched hands. He understood that greed would quench the holy fire forever, while true honor demanded that the harvest be shared equally. With reverence, Vael divided the radiant flames, returning half the light across the winds to Sola so her hearth would glow with eight bright embers, while keeping seven to illuminate the fertile valley below.

Though the capricious mountain gales sometimes carried away a stray spark in flight, neither keeper allowed fear or suspicion to cloud their bond. Sola continued to cast all five embers without hesitation, and Vael unfailingly returned a generous half of the bounty. Through unwavering trust and just return, the celestial flame burned eternal, proving that shared abundance is the highest wisdom of heaven and earth.

Each morning, Sola gathered her full measure of five celestial sparks and hurled them across the howling abyss without hesitation.
